orientation.batter_faces: East-southeast (approximately 120 degrees). Home plate sits at the northwest corner of the block near 35th St & Shields Ave; the batter looks out toward center field to the east-southeast. The third-base/left-field side of the park faces roughly south-southwest and the first-base/right-field side faces roughly north-northeast (which is why the first-base side gets the best afternoon shade).
orientation.corroborating_source: https://tht.fangraphs.com/lost-in-the-sun-the-physics-of-ballpark-orientation/ -- 'they still wanted home plate at 35th and Shields, so the ballpark now points Southeast.' Also corroborated by mlb.com Hidden Gems placing Gate 5 and the Old Comiskey home plate marker on the NORTH side at 35th & Shields.
orientation.verbatim: "Home plate faces west-northwest and center field points toward the east-southeast." -- theshadium.com
orientation.note: This is an unusual orientation for MLB (most parks point north/northeast). Do not assume the league-typical NE heading for this park.

numbering_direction.summary: MOST IMPORTANT FIELD: Section numbers INCREASE toward THIRD BASE / LEFT FIELD. On every level, the LOW numbers start in RIGHT FIELD / down the right-field line, run counterclockwise (as seen on a standard overhead seating chart) through the first-base side, past home plate in the middle of the range, on through the third-base side, and terminate with the HIGH numbers in LEFT FIELD / LEFT-CENTER FIELD. Concretely on the 100 Level: 100-105 = right field, 122-127 = visiting dugout (first-base side), 130-134 = directly behind home plate, 137-142 = White Sox dugout (third-base side), 157-159 = left field, 160-164 = left-center-field bleachers. The same low-to-high right-to-left progression holds on the 300 Level (311 down the right-field line to 357 down the left-field line) and the 500 Level.

accessibility.summary: Wheelchair-accessible seating is located on ALL levels. On the Main (100) Level the accessible sections are 104, 109, 110, 118, 119, 133, 144, 145, 154, 155 and 160. Verbatim: "All of the accessible seats on the Club (300) and Upper (500) Levels are sightline-accessible," and the Diamond Suite levels are accessible as well. Companion seating is available adjacent to wheelchair spaces based on availability. Separately, individual section pages on RateYourSeats show a dedicated row labeled 'WCH' at the back of many 100-Level sections (e.g. Section 140 rows are '5-35, WCH'; Section 160 row WCH has 12 seats labeled 1-12; Section 120 row WCH has 5 seats labeled 1-5) -- the WCH row is the wheelchair/companion platform row and is always the last row listed for a section. Electric wheelchair charging and sign-language interpreters are available on advance request at 312-674-5225 (or 312-674-5188 TDD). Wheelchair escorts to seats are provided at gate entrances but cannot enter the parking lots. Service animals are welcome.

discovery.row_seat_conventions: ROWS ARE NUMBERS, not letters -- this is the dominant convention at Rate Field on every level. Examples: Section 100 rows 1-25; Section 101 rows '1-28, WCH'; Section 105 rows '9-28, WCH'; Section 120 rows '1-35, WCH'; Section 132 rows '16-35, WCH'; Section 140 rows '5-35, WCH'; Section 158 rows '8-28, WCH'; Section 160 rows '1-26, WCH'; Section 311 rows 1-5; Section 334 'The first row in this section is labeled 1' (five rows total); Sections 530/534 rows 1-21. TWO EXCEPTIONS TO WATCH FOR: (1) a trailing alphabetic row 'WCH' -- the wheelchair/companion row -- appears as the LAST row in most 100-Level sections; (2) a leading double-letter row can precede row 1 in a few lower-bowl sections, e.g. Section 152 rows are labeled 'AA, 1-35, WCH', where AA sits IN FRONT of row 1. Row 1 is the row closest to the field except where an AA row exists. Seat counts per row grow as you move back (e.g. Section 160: rows 1-6 have 16 seats, rows 7-18 have 17, rows 19-26 have 18).
discovery.seat1_side_verbatim: "When looking towards the field, lower number seats are on the right" -- RateYourSeats.com, stated identically on the Rate Field pages for Section 100, Section 101, Section 105, Section 109, Section 140 and Section 163. Practical reading: seat 1 is on the RIGHT-hand aisle when you are seated facing the field (i.e. seat numbers increase from right to left as you look at the diamond). CAUTION: a user review on the Section 140 page states the opposite for one row -- "When facing the field, seat 1 is on the left aisle" (Row 7) -- but that is fan-submitted comment text, not the site's section rule; the authoritative site-wide statement is the 'lower number seats are on the right' line, which is repeated verbatim across every section page checked.
discovery.known_obstructions: 1) THE STEEP/HIGH UPPER DECK is this park's signature problem. Verbatim from Wikipedia: "The first row of seats in the upper deck of the new stadium is as far from the field as the old stadium's highest row," and it was "one of the highest upper decks in baseball." RateYourSeats section pages warn: "Because of the stadium's vertical design, the upper level sits high above the field with steep walkways." A fan note on Section 534: "Although these are front row they are very high above the field." The 2003 Phase III renovation demolished the top EIGHT rows (about 6,600 seats) off the upper deck to lower the structure, and replaced the sloped canopy roof with a flat roof elevated 20 feet above the seating area that now covers roughly two-thirds of the upper deck. Vertigo and fear-of-heights complaints in the 500 Level are common; the first few rows of 500-Level sections can also have a RAILING in the sightline -- fan note on Section 534: "The first few rows in this section may have an issue with the railing -- it was a slight disruption for our view." 2) OUTFIELD WALL / FAN DECK OBSTRUCTIONS: sections 163 and 164 (left-center bleachers) lose part of the outfield -- verbatim: "Sections closest to the center-field Fan Deck (163,164) can have more limited views of parts of the outfield due to the Fan Deck structure and outfield wall." The Stadium Insiders flags the same problem in sections 100-101 (right field) as well as 163-164. 3) ACCESS RESTRICTION (not a sightline issue but affects seat value): the White Sox are the only MLB club that prohibits 300- and 500-Level ticket holders from entering the 100 Level concourse at all. 4) The 300 Level is only about five rows deep in many sections, so 300-Level seats sit close to the front rail; the deck above can cut off high fly balls in the rearmost 100-Level rows.
uncertain: Concert-only sections: none could be confirmed. RateYourSeats has no concert configuration page for Rate Field and AViewFromMySeat's concert chart does not enumerate floor sections. Any concert floor/GA-pit sections would be event-specific.

Full 300- and 500-Level section rings: The Stadium Insiders lists the 300 Level as 'Sections 301-359' and the 500 Level as 'Sections 501-559' (continuous rings), while RateYourSeats enumerates only the baseball-ticketed subsets 311-357 and 506-558. Sections 301-310, 358-359, 501-505 and 559 are likely suite/service/non-public space but this was not directly confirmed.

The 300 Level's official name: MLB and The Stadium Insiders call it the 'Club Level'; one RateYourSeats page rendering labeled it 'Mezzanine Level' and another swapped the 300/500 level labels entirely. 'Club Level' (300) and 'Upper Level' (500) is the correct pairing per the White Sox' own disability guide, which names them 'Club (300)' and 'Upper (500)'.

Sections 106 and 107 do not exist as ticketed seating -- that arc is occupied by the Miller Lite Landing. The mlb.com accessibility guide nonetheless references a companion restroom 'near section 106,' which should be read as the Miller Lite Landing area in right field.

Compass orientation is sourced from theshadium.com plus a corroborating comment on tht.fangraphs.com rather than from an official White Sox or MLB publication; the ~120-degree figure should be treated as approximate.

Exact current capacity for the 2026 season: 40,615 is the long-standing published figure, but recent ticketing sites sometimes cite slightly lower numbers (~40,300) after minor premium-space conversions. No 2026-specific official figure was found.
Whether the Bullpen Sports Bar still operates under that name after the Rate Field rebrand was not verified.

Scout Seats sponsor naming is inconsistent across sources ('Wintrust Scout Seats' on Wikipedia vs 'CIBC Scout Club' on The Stadium Insiders); the section labels 130S/131S/133S/134S are stable regardless.
RateYourSeats still labels the 300-Level premium club 'Guaranteed Rate Club' on its sections index -- this is stale branding for what the team now calls the Rate Field Club.
